images.title: The three countries do not make the World count
images.purpose: Shows that in 2024 the United States, China and Russia together are about 200 short of the World count.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Two tall columns side by side for the year 2024: a World column on the left and a stacked column of the three countries on the right, with the gap at the top marked.
images.exact_structure: A short baseline with the label 2024 under it. Left column: one grey (#6B7280) outlined column with light grey fill reaching about 2850, labelled World about 2850 beside its top. Right column, same width: a stack of three parts from the bottom, teal (#0072B2) up to about 2250 labelled United States about 2250, then a thin amber (#E69F00) part of about 280 labelled China about 280, then a thinner vermilion (#D55E00) part of about 120 labelled Russia about 120, reaching about 2650. Above the stack, an empty dashed grey outline from about 2650 up to the World height of about 2850, labelled about 200 not shown. No vertical scale numbers.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: The three countries add to about 2650, so about 200 objects come from countries the graph does not show.
images.description: Shows that in 2024 the United States, China and Russia together are about 200 short of the World count.
images.context: 2250 + 280 + 120 = 2650; 2850 − 2650 = 200. Values approximate, read from the line graph.

image_decisions.why: Putting the three countries side by side with the World count makes the step two inference visible: other countries are missing.
